messages:
maya: Hey, h100 CI job `job/ci-h100-98765` turned red on master during warmup — OOM. Logs show cuda allocation failures but nvidia-smi reports free memory. Can someone take a quick look? cc @sam @linh

maya: log snippet:
```
E runtime: cuMemAllocAsync failed: out of memory
allocated: 12.0GiB, attempted alloc: 512.0MiB
GPU0: 18.4GiB free / 80.0GiB total (seen via nvidia-smi)
stack: <truncated> at inference::workspace::alloc
```

sam: Can you paste the node driver info and a full nvidia-smi -q? Also were there other pods on the same node at the time? If driver/kernel mismatch or other tenants holding pinned allocations that could explain it.

linh: nvidia-smi -q from the node (just the top bits):
```
Driver Version                        : 535.54.03
CUDA Version                          : 12.2
Attached GPUs                         : 8
Processes                             : python (PID 4123)  / model-runner
```
No obvious extra tenant on that node in the last 10m.

maya: I reran the job once and it failed the same way. kubectl logs show repeated small frees then a big failure at warmup: `cuMemAllocAsync failed` (see above).

infra-bot: Rerun triggered by @maya: https://redwood.ci/runs/98765 (queued) :arrows_counterclockwise:

sam: Two quick experiments to narrow this down: 1) enable allocation tracing so we can see per-allocation sizes/backtraces (set `REDWOOD_GPU_ALLOC_TRACE=1` in the job env) and re-run, 2) toggle CUDA async allocator (`CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC=0`) to see if fragmentation goes away. The trace will tell us if there are many mid-sized frees causing fragmentation or a single large persistent allocation starving the pool.

ekaterina: I pulled the alloc trace we uploaded (s3://redwood-internal/traces/98765/alloc_trace.txt) — pattern looks like many ~256KiB allocations interleaved with a few 8–12GiB persistent allocations. That smells like fragmentation: a lot of small churn prevents the large contiguous chunk needed for workspace. Short-term mitigation: set SMALL_BATCHES=true or reduce workspace preallocation so the big workspace is smaller. Longer term: we should try a different driver build — we've seen similar fragmentation on 535.x for some H100 configs; candidate drivers to test: 536.x or fallback to 530.x (canary only).

maya: thanks — i'll open a small PR to bump the driver on the h100 canary pool and add `REDWOOD_GPU_ALLOC_TRACE=1` to the failing CI job so we get traces by default for this suite. Scheduling the canary run for tomorrow morning.

sam: SGTM. if canary fixes it we can rollout to dedicated. If not, the trace will help us bisect whether it's runtime allocator or kernel/driver behavior. :thumbsup:

maya: noted, will update after canary. thanks all :pray:
